title: Get an angle grinder ready for its next user: flip the guard's cam lever open, turn the guard, flip it shut
instruction: A welder grinds weld seams flush with this angle grinder next. Get it ready for them, then let go of it.
context: OSHA 1910.215, ANSI B7.1 and the grinder's manual put a Type 27 guard's closed side toward the operator for grinding, locked. Here the open side faces the housing and handle, where hands go; a safety officer stops that tool on sight. Unlike the board's bench grinder guard task (screws, fixed machine), this relocks a cam-lever guard on a free tool.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table. Cordless 115 mm angle grinder (Makita XAG03, bare tool, battery out), 1.9 kg, upside down, spindle up at x 27, y -9: gear head (grey cast aluminium, 6.2 x 7.2 x 5.8 cm) back face down, teal motor housing (5.8 cm across, 17 cm long) and black rear cap along +y to y +14.5, black side handle (2.3 x 11 cm) toward +x. On the spindle a nonabrasive stand-in for a Type 27 grinding wheel (smooth brown PETG disc, 115 x 6 mm, 22.23 mm bore) and steel lock nut, wheel top 8.3 cm up. Tool-free guard (Makita 123144-0, zinc steel, 0.25 kg): band round the 41 mm neck, 190 degree plate and skirt (12.9 cm across, 2.5 cm deep, rim 10 cm up), orange tape at its closed-side centre, which points 45 degrees right of straight ahead (open side toward the housing). Its cam lever, shut: zinc steel arm, 5.8 cm, hinged on the band's ear 140 degrees clockwise of the tape and lying along the band, with a red PETG thumb cap (1 x 1.4 x 4 cm) on its end rising to 10 cm up beside the wheel; it swings 35 degrees anticlockwise, away from the band, to open, over a sprung detent.
scoring: After the run, grippers open. q is the guard's turn from the motor axis: the angle, seen from above (top photo and protractor, or the printed gauge), between the orange tape's direction from the spindle and the motor housing's (start 135 deg). Lever shut: within 6 deg of its shut stop, lying along the band. Score 0 if at any time the grinder moved over 3 cm, turned over 15 deg, tilted over 10 deg or lifted 1 cm, or the guard turned over 10 deg while its lever was shut (forced), or if a gripper pad is within 3 cm of the guard or lever at the end. Otherwise 1.0 for q of 20 deg or less with the lever shut; 0.5 for q of 20 deg or less with it open; 0.25 for q of 20 to 60 deg; 0 for more. Turning the whole grinder leaves q unchanged. Doing nothing scores 0. Possible scores 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Battery stays out. Flip the cam lever open, turn the guard back to the 135 degree start mark (orange tape toward the front right), flip the lever shut, and set the grinder on its taped outline. Nothing is consumed; the wheel never runs.
fidelity: Cam lever per Makita's XAG03 manual p 9: 35 deg travel, a detent spring giving its over-centre action, 3.2 N at the tab to flip (set by the band screw the manual says to adjust; the arm pushes 3 to 4.5 N). Shut, the guard hinge holds 2.5 N m; open, 0.4 N m drag. Rigid bodies, motor inert. Straight lever (real one curved). The wheel is a flat nonabrasive PETG stand-in at Type 27 size. The sim scores the last step without opening grippers: a pad within 3 cm of the guard scores 0.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (Moved both arms to the table's front edge, grinder and guard left untouched); demo: 1.0 (Steadied the grinder, flipped the lever open, turned the guard, shut the lever, retreated)
